🧠 Crypto News Brief: August opened on the back foot: bitcoin hovers near $63K after a hawkish Fed and month-end ETF outflows, while a $70M hardware-wallet exploit and a $676M sanctions probe kept sentiment defensive and risk-aware. 🔓 Coldcard Firmware Flaw Drains ~$70M in Bitcoin Without Touching a Single Device A firmware bug dating to March 2021 caused certain Coldcard hardware wallets to generate recovery seeds using predictable software randomness instead of the chip's hardware RNG, letting an attacker reconstruct private keys entirely offline. Galaxy Research mapped a 41-minute sweep on July 30 that drained 1,082 BTC from 1,196 wallets across six blocks. Maker Coinkite has shipped patched firmware, but seeds already created on vulnerable versions can't be repaired, and users are urged to migrate funds immediately. Read full story 🕵️ Reuters: Iran-Linked Dubai Exchange Shelbit Routed $676M to Binance A Reuters investigation traced at least $676 million from wallets tied to Shelbit — an unlicensed Dubai exchange — into Binance since May 2024, roughly $540 million of it after Dubai's VARA fined the operation. Shelbit allegedly processed over $4 billion, connecting a Farsi-language gambling network, Iran's central bank and IRGC-linked entities. Binance says Shelbit never held an account and that flagged users were frozen and reported to law enforcement. More details 🏦 Saylor's Strategy Abandons Its "All-In Bitcoin" Rule, Will Keep Selling BTC On its Q2 earnings call, Strategy confirmed it will no longer funnel every dollar of new capital into bitcoin and will sell BTC opportunistically to fund dividends and buybacks, splitting proceeds dynamically between bitcoin and USD reserves. The pivot follows a multi-billion-dollar unrealized loss last quarter; analysts say management is now focused on restoring its STRC preferred shares toward par. The firm still bought far more BTC than it sold across 2026. Read more 💵 Tether Posts $1.5B Q2 Profit — But Its Excess Reserve Cushion Halves to $4.1B Tether's BDO attestation showed $1.5 billion in net operating profit for Q2, driven by U.S. Treasury and repo returns, with USDT supply near $184.6B and over 60% stablecoin market share.
